fields.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
fields.note: The requirement summary tracks §§ 98.0704–98.0708: at-fault and no-fault causes, notices, relocation assistance, right of first offer, Commission notice delay, buyouts, and retaliation. Voiding of the notice is in §§ 98.0706(e) and 98.0710.

fields.quoted_span: the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to two months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
fields.note: Three months for seniors or disabled tenants is in § 98.0706(c)(1)(A)(ii). The 15-day payment, rent waiver option, 5-year offer right with 30 days to accept, 3x damages in § 98.0709(d) and (e), and buyouts exceeding relocation assistance in § 98.0707(d) are all in the text.

fields.quoted_span: (“Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy” added 5-25-2023 by O-21647 N.S.; effective 6-24-2023.)
fields.note: Effective 6-24-2023 is confirmed, and the amendment effective 3-28-2024 is also shown.
The text is the 3-2024 edition and shows no repeal or sunset, which is consistent with in_force. The document cannot confirm that it is currently in force beyond that edition.

fields.quoted_span: (k) housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome; and
fields.note: The exemptions in § 98.0703(a)–(l), the definitions of residential rental property and tenancy, and the Section 8 carve-out all match. The two-unit owner-occupied and single-family owner-occupied exemptions are accurately described.

fields.note: The section is correctly cited. The aliases (Division 7, §§ 98.0701–98.0710, O-21647, O-21769, O-19269, and the tenants' right to know title) all appear in the text.
